claim: Le Panier is Marseille's oldest district, settled by Greeks from Phocaea around 600 BC, now an artists' quarter of winding pedestrian alleys with bistros, craftsmen, antique dealers and concept stores.
quote: Le Panier: The Artists' District, a must in Marseille

claim: Street art is everywhere in Le Panier - collages, murals and stencils - and street art took root in Marseille in the 1980s with hip-hop culture; the Vieille Charite sits at the heart of the neighbourhood.
quote: Street art naturally took root in Marseilles in the 1980s with the advent of hip-hop culture

claim: Cours Julien is the largest district in France dedicated to street art, an artists' quarter packed with murals, indie boutiques, cafes and lively bars.
quote: the artists' and street art district

claim: Cours Julien and La Plaine (6th arrondissement) form Marseille's bohemian, lively core; the Place Jean Jaures market runs four days a week (Tue, Thu, Sat, with Wednesday for flowers) and the area shines after dark with bars and nightlife.
quote: Cours Julien truly shines after dark, offering a lively and energetic nightlife scene

claim: Notre-Dame-du-Mont came out on top in Time Out's annual ranking of the coolest neighbourhoods in the world; it offers drag bars, club nights, brunches and galleries amid an eclectic mix of hipsters and old-school locals.
quote: came out on top ... annual rankings of the coolest neighbourhoods in the world

claim: The Vallon des Auffes - Corniche circuit runs about 10.8 km (roughly 2 hours) from Catalan Beach along the Corniche Kennedy to the Prado, passing the picturesque Vallon des Auffes fishing port and the 3km 'longest bench in the world' with views of the Frioul islands.
quote: a small fishing port that has remained traditional

claim: The Corniche Kennedy seaside promenade extends about 3.7km from Catalans Beach near the Vieux-Port to the Prado beaches, with a 2km cycle path and pavements suited to pushchairs and reduced-mobility visitors.
The OM Tour is a self-guided behind-the-scenes visit of the Orange Velodrome giving access to the players' locker room, players' tunnel, dugout, pitchside and trophy room, lasting roughly 1.5 hours.
quote: OM TOUR - Visit the Orange Velodrome Stadium

claim: The Orange Velodrome holds about 67,000 spectators, making it France's second-largest stadium, a hub of sport for over 80 years that has hosted World Cup matches and major concerts; visitors praise its iconic roof and electrifying matchday atmosphere.
quote: impressive seating capacity of 67,000 making it France's second-largest stadium

claim: Notre-Dame du Mont is Marseille's edgy, artsy nightlife neighbourhood in the heights of the 6th arrondissement, rougher around the edges than other areas, with legally-tagged street-art walls, vintage shops and underground bars.
quote: Notre Dame du Mont in Marseille - Marseille's Edgy Nightlife Neighbourhood

claim: Endoume, southwest of the centre along the water, is a picturesque residential area of rocky bays, cliffside swimming spots and secluded coves, best explored by bike along the Corniche Kennedy.
quote: Endoume offers visitors a picturesque beach experience with plenty of rocky bays
